item.title: California Native Creations Art Show — Thu Sep 10, 8:30 AM — Person Senior Wing
item.description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.
The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:
· Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,
· Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,
· Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,
· Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.
· plus Gloria Car

item.title: Formative Influence Art Exhibit — Thu Sep 10, 9:00 AM — Marin Center
item.description:
Formative Influence explores the transformative power of light across five bodies of work. Inspired by the landscapes of Northern California and the American West, the exhibition examines the shift from photography, where light is observed and captured, to painting, where light is created to shape new visual experiences. Rather than documenting the landscape, these works evoke its emotional resonance, emphasizing atmosphere, memory, and perception over literal representation.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Visiting Artist Lecture Series at Sonoma State University — Thu Sep 10, 12:00 PM — D
item.description:
The Visiting Artist Lecture Series is hosted by the art studio program at Sonoma State University. This series brings in local artists to talk about their work and experiences. September 10 - Chanell Stone \(b. Los Angeles\) is an artist living and working in Oakland, California. Her practice examines the phenomenology of the female body as both a geographic site and physical material embedded within the American landscape. Grounded in the interdisciplinary frameworks of Black feminist thought and image-based media, Stone theorizes how memory and place are inscribed onto and throughout the body. Her inquiries take form through photography, poetry and material-based exploration, wherein she engages with lesser-known impressions of Black American presence and belonging.
Source: Creative Sonoma, North Bay Bohemian

item.description:

This is a free event, but reserving your tickets assists us with planning.
A Good Year was directed by Ridley Scott and stars Russell Crowe and Abbie Cornish. item.title: Guided Nature Walk & Ranch House tour Anderson Marsh — Sat Sep 12, 8:30 AM — Anderson Marsh State Historic Park
item.description:
The next “Second Saturday” Guided Nature walk at Anderson Marsh State Historic Park will be held on Saturday, September 12, 2026.
The Guided Walk will begin at 8:30am. Bring binoculars and meet in the parking lot at 8:15am for an opportunity to observe the birds and other wildlife found in the picnic area. Sturdy shoes, a hat and water are suggested.
The September guided walk will be led by State Parks volunteer docent Roberta Lyons and will provide an opportunity to observe wildlife at the park and learn about their natural habitat, as well as to learn about the natural and cultural history of the area.
The walk will take between 1½ and 2 hours, depending on the route taken. Dogs are not allowed on the park trails.
A tour of the historic Anderson Ranch House will be available immediately after the conclusion of the walk.
There is no charge for the Nature Walk and Ranch House tour and parking is free for those attending.
Source: Press Democrat

item.description:
The Vallejo Kite Festival returns for our third year at the beautiful Barbara Kondylis Waterfront Green on September 12th. This free Festival invites all Vallejo and Bay Area residents to join us in flying kites! Our main attraction is a collection of large, professional kites flown by The Kite Man of Martinez. These kites have been flown around the world, from Europe to Asia, and we’re privileged to have them flown in Vallejo! We’ll have owls, birds, and dragons filling up the sky; this is something you don’t want to miss!
The Vallejo Kite Festival is also bringing back the incredible partnership of InflataBill and 707Drones for our VR Hot Air Balloon Experience! See the waterfront and all our kites from high up in the sky without ever leaving the comfort of the ground! Sit in a handcrafted hot air balloon basket, put on a VR headset, and take flight with our professionally operated drone cameras!

item.title: Live Music Saturday: The Northern Still — Sat Sep 12, 6:00 PM — Ferry Taproom
item.description:
Dawn Angelosante’s \(piano\) voice wraps lyrics into a dreamscape of sound and story, touching on love, friendship, heartbreak, and self-reflection. Tony Gibson’s \(guitar\) songwriting blends infectious melodies with honest, emotionally resonant lyrics. His music feels familiar and fresh. Michael Fecskes \(cello\), a classically trained cellist and composer, adds a unique depth to the group’s sound. His compositions are rich and soulful.
Together, they form The Northern Still, a dynamic acoustic/folk-pop trio. Since 2021 they’ve combined their individual voices and musical influences into a lush, intimate sound, with haunting vocal harmonies. Whether performing original compositions or their fresh takes on covers, they’ve captivated audiences throughout the North Bay.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Sep 13, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.
Source: North Bay Bohemian
